features.title: Open a thread in the right side panel
features.summary: A thread's row context menu, its hover action, the Open in side panel command palette action and a `@dshfiles/main-tabs` thread tab's own context menu open that thread in the right sidebar instead of the main column: the row action routes through the entry's sidebar-right controller, which opens a threadaside resource tab, and the tab menu asks for the same aside over the cancelable `dshfiles:open-thread-aside` window event this plugin answers. Dragging a main thread tab onto the open side panel moves it here the same way, and the aside tab's own menu row Move to main area hands it back: it dispatches `dshfiles:open-thread` and closes the aside only once `@dshfiles/main-tabs` took the thread, so the thread lives in one place. The tab retains the Session and hosts the same embedded Conversation a subagent chat does, so the thread streams and its composer works beside the thread the user is reading; closing the tab only releases the reference, and an already-open aside is focused instead of duplicated. The rebindable command threadSidebar.openInSidePanel ships unbound, and Customize sidebar > Hover actions stores hiddenRowActions and rowActionOrder so every row button is per-user in both visibility and left-to-right order.

features.title: Continue a thread in another project
features.summary: A thread started in the wrong folder, or whose work moved to another repository, continues in a registered project: the row menu and the thread header menu open a Continue in project submenu listing the projects, and the agent tool thread_continue_in does the same. The conversation is forked into a new thread whose own working directory is that project's workspace (its isolated jj workspace when jj-integration isolates new threads), the new thread is told where it came from, the original thread is settled so it stays readable but runs no further step, and the new thread opens. An agent continuing its own thread keeps its running turn in the copy and stops after the call.
failureModes: Another thread that is still running is refused before anything is created; only the calling thread may continue mid-turn.
An unknown project is refused before a thread is created, and the original is not settled.
A continuation whose original cannot be settled is still reported, with a warning instead of a hidden thread id.
A Host without the session-controller continuation API shows the restart hint in the submenu instead of failing the row menu.
